Internal types (upstream's operator classes and their sinks, the internal helpers) are implementation; they count only through their files, which are ported one to one. Overloads are found by name: every overload of a method counts as present once the Rust function of its name in snake case exists, or that name with a suffix (`_on` for a scheduler argument, `_with`, `_with_index`, ...) or the `try_` prefix. The methods a `*_methods!` macro writes into a trait or an `impl` count as methods of that trait or type. An upstream file without a Rust file at its own path is present in the Rust files whose module documentation (the leading `//!` lines) cites it, such as `Linq/Observable/Select.cs`. A missing file whose types are all waived counts as a waived file.
